after.title: CVE-2026-135641 (critical 9.1): The WP Job Portal – AI-Powered Recruitment System for Company or Job Board website plugin for WordPress is vulnerable
after.summary: The WP Job Portal – AI-Powered Recruitment System for Company or Job Board website plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 2.7.2 This is due to a flaw in `WPJOBPORTALuser::__construct()` where the non-empty guard on the `wpjobportal-socialid` cookie is evaluated against the raw cookie value before `sanitize_key()` is applied — allowing a value composed entirely of characters outside `[a-z0-9_-]` to pass the guard, be reduced to an empty string by `sanitize_key()`, and be used as the literal value in a `WHERE socialid = ''` database query that matches the first portal account whose `socialid` column is empty. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to be bound to an existing WP Job Portal Employer or Jobseeker account, gaining the ability to create, edit, and delete the victim's companies, job listings, resumes, and applications, as well as overwrite the linked WordPress user's first name, last name, and display name via the `saveuser`→`syncWPUserName()` path. Exploitation is viable on virtually all installations because every portal account not registered through the social-login flow retains the default empty `socialid` value; nonce checks on downstream actions such as `savecompany` and `saveuser` do not mitigate this issue because those nonces are minted within the already-hijacked session and validate against the attacker's own subsequent requests. Successful exploitation gives the attacker control of a distinct, already-privileged WP Job Portal Employer / Jobseeker (bound to a specific WordPress user) account; it does not promote the attacker's original account.

after.summary: The Simple Membership plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.8.9 This is due to the site-wide signing secret `swpm_private_key_one` being generated at install time with PHP's non-cryptographic `uniqid('', true)` function in `SwpmInstallation::installer()`, whose timestamp-derived keyspace (~10^15 candidates / ~50 bits) can be constrained via the public WordPress REST API date of the plugin's auto-created registration page, combined with a single-MD5 oracle (`md5(key|level)`) that the public registration form prints as `swpm_level_hash` and a non-constant-time `!=` comparison in `SwpmFrontRegistration::register_front_end()` as the sole authorization gate on which membership level a visitor may register into; `SwpmUtils::get_free_level()` then honors an attacker-posted `level_identifier=md5(level)` regardless of the configured free-membership setting, and `prepare_and_create_wp_user_front_end()` creates the WordPress account with whatever role the level is configured to grant (only the `administrator` role is refused). after.summary: The Product Input Fields for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.0 via the process_file_input_field function. This is due to missing file type validation in the process_file_input_field function, which accepts the client-supplied multipart Content-Type header as the sole type gate and writes the uploaded file to the unprotected pif_temp directory using the verbatim client-supplied filename. after.summary: Several plugins for WordPress published by WP connect (Orders Sync to Airtable for WooCommerce, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Notion, WP Sync for Notion – Notion to WordPress, Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Airtable, Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms, and Air WP Sync – Airtable to WordPress) contain embedded malicious code (a backdoor) in the versions listed. The affected releases unconditionally load a backdoor module (includes/airwp-online.php) that runs on every request via the 'init' hook and on a half-hourly WP-Cron event, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress and OS versions, and the server user) to a remote command-and-control server at tascredit-pay.com with TLS certificate verification disabled, and executes the PHP code returned by that server via eval(). The module also accepts queued commands that run shell commands, read, write and delete arbitrary files, query arbitrary database tables, dump the users table including password hashes, drop a webshell into the uploads directory, and install persistent hourly code execution. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers in control of the remote server, or able to intercept its traffic, to execute arbitrary code on the server and fully compromise affected sites. All affected plugins have been closed on WordPress.org and no patched versions are available; we strongly recommend uninstalling them and running a complete malware scan.
